issues.title: Test file not co-located with component
issues.description: The rule requires test files to be in the same directory as component files. The test file flow-icon-text.test.tsx was moved to a __tests__ subdirectory instead of being co-located with flow-icon-text.tsx in the same directory.
issues.rule_name: React Component Test Files Must Be Co-Located

issues.title: QueryClient instance mismatch between router context and provider
issues.description: The Storybook decorator creates a QueryClient instance mismatch. The `createTestRouter` function instantiates a new QueryClient (`new QueryClient()`) and passes it to the router context on line 32. However, the decorator wraps the component with `QueryClientProvider` using the module-level `queryClient` instance on line 43. This creates two separate QueryClient instances - one for the router context and one for the provider. Queries executed within the router tree will use a different cache than queries executed through the provider, causing cache inconsistency and potential state synchronization issues. The router and provider should share the same QueryClient instance.

issues.title: Missing Suspense fallback causes blank UI during loading
issues.description: The FlowIconText component wraps FlowIconTextImplementation in a Suspense boundary but doesn't provide a fallback prop. When the component suspends while fetching flow data via useSuspenseQuery, React has no fallback content to display, resulting in a blank space in the UI until the query resolves. This creates a poor user experience with no loading indicator. The original implementation should have included a fallback prop like `<Skeleton className="h-4 w-full" />` to show a loading state during data fetching.

issues.title: Unused import violates Rule #12 noUnusedImports configuration
issues.description: The flow-icon-text.tsx file imports Skeleton from '@/components/ui/skeleton' on line 6 but never uses it in the component code. This directly violates Rule #12 'Unused Imports Must Be Automatically Removed' from AGENTS.md, which requires that unused imports be eliminated via automated linting. The biome.json configuration explicitly sets noUnusedImports as an error, meaning this should have been caught by pre-commit hooks. The unused import increases bundle size unnecessarily and indicates the linting process was bypassed or failed.

issues.title: Unused import: Skeleton
issues.description: `Skeleton` is imported but never used in this file, which violates the rule requiring unused imports to be removed.
issues.rule_name: Unused Imports Must Be Automatically Removed

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #20030 - Add FlowIconText component for UI v2 migration

structured_output.summary:
This PR adds a `FlowIconText` component in `ui-v2/src/components/flows/flow-icon-text/`. It fetches a flow by ID with `useSuspenseQuery(buildFLowDetailsQuery(...))` and renders the Workflow icon plus flow name as a link to `/flows/flow/$id`. Unlike `FlowLink`, it omits the "Flow" label. The component follows the existing `FlowLink` pattern and the route, icon, and query helper it uses all exist.

The implementation is small and mostly correct, but the change is not ready to merge. The PR description and checklist say a unit test file (`flow-icon-text.test.tsx`) was added, but it is not in the diff and does not exist on the head commit. The component also imports `Skeleton` without using it, and it drops the skeleton fallback that the description and `FlowLink` both rely on, so the loading state renders nothing.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The missing test file contradicts the PR's checklist, and this is a new component with no coverage. The unused import will likely trip the lint/typecheck gate. The Suspense fallback is missing relative to both the description and `FlowLink`, which changes the loading UX. None of these are deep design problems, so they should be straightforward to fix before merge.

architecture.overview:
The existing flow-linking UI goes through `FlowLink` (`ui-v2/src/components/flows/flow-link.tsx`). That component wraps a suspense-backed inner implementation around `useSuspenseQuery(buildFLowDetailsQuery(flowId))` from `@/api/flows`. It renders a "Flow" label followed by a TanStack `Link` to the `/flows/flow/$id` route, which is defined in `src/routes/flows/flow.$id.tsx`. `FlowLink` is used by callers such as `deployment-links.tsx` and `trigger-details-flow-run-state.tsx`.

This PR adds a sibling component, `FlowIconText`, in its own folder with an index re-export. It uses the same query, route, and `Icon id="Workflow"` as `FlowLink`, but renders only the icon and name. Its own `Suspense` boundary is a bare `<Suspense>` with no fallback, so while the query is pending nothing is rendered. Nothing in the repo calls `FlowIconText` yet, and the new test file is absent.
steps: Entry point: callers pass a `flowId` to `FlowIconText` (`ui-v2/src/components/flows/flow-icon-text/flow-icon-text.tsx`), either directly or through the `index.ts` re-export.

The outer `FlowIconText` wraps `FlowIconTextImplementation` in a `Suspense` boundary. Per the PR description and `FlowLink`, this boundary should have a `Skeleton` fallback, but the current code omits it.
`FlowIconTextImplementation` calls `useSuspenseQuery(buildFLowDetailsQuery(flowId))` from `@/api/flows`. This is the same data path `FlowLink` uses.

The rendered output is a TanStack `Link` to `/flows/flow/$id` (route in `src/routes/flows/flow.$id.tsx`) containing `Icon id="Workflow"` and `flow.name`. Compared with `FlowLink`, the only change is the removal of the "Flow" text label.

Storybook (`flow-icon-text.stories.tsx`) builds its own memory router and `QueryClientProvider` in a decorator to render the component. The unit test (`flow-icon-text.test.tsx`) is described as MSW-based but is not present in the head commit.

findings.title: Test file claimed in PR description is missing from the diff
findings.body:
The PR description and checklist say `flow-icon-text.test.tsx` is added with MSW-based unit tests, and the checklist marks "includes unit tests" as done. The diff only contains `flow-icon-text.stories.tsx`, `flow-icon-text.tsx`, and `index.ts`. On the head commit the `flow-icon-text/` folder holds just those three files, so the component has no test coverage at all.

The sibling `deployment-link.tsx` ships with `deployment-link.test.tsx`, which is the pattern to follow. A test should check at least:
- the rendered name and icon once the query resolves
- that the `href` points at `/flows/flow/<id>`
- the loading state (see the Suspense finding)
- what happens on a 404 or query error (the error bubbles to the nearest error boundary, as with `FlowLink`)

::file{file="ui-v2/src/components/flows/flow-icon-text/flow-icon-text.tsx"}
findings.fixPrompt: Add the missing unit test file `ui-v2/src/components/flows/flow-icon-text/flow-icon-text.test.tsx`, which the PR description says is included but is absent from the diff. Follow the MSW and render setup in `ui-v2/src/components/deployments/deployment-link.test.tsx`. Cover the rendered flow name and Workflow icon after the query resolves, the link `href` `/flows/flow/<id>`, and the pending/loading state. Keep assertions on observable DOM output, not on internal query calls.

findings.title: Unused `Skeleton` import left over from the copied FlowLink pattern
findings.fixPrompt: In `ui-v2/src/components/flows/flow-icon-text/flow-icon-text.tsx`, the `Skeleton` import on line 6 is currently unused. Resolve it by adding a fallback to the `Suspense` boundary in `FlowIconText` (see the related finding about the missing fallback). That will make the import used. If the fallback is not added, remove the import instead. Run the ui-v2 lint and typecheck afterward.

findings.title: Missing Suspense fallback causes blank render and contradicts the description
findings.fixPrompt: In `ui-v2/src/components/flows/flow-icon-text/flow-icon-text.tsx`, the `Suspense` in `FlowIconText` (around line 12) has no fallback. Add `fallback={<Skeleton className="h-4 w-full" />}`, matching `FlowLink` in `ui-v2/src/components/flows/flow-link.tsx`. This also makes the existing `Skeleton` import used. Add a test that confirms the skeleton renders while the query is pending.

findings.title: Storybook router creates an unused second QueryClient
findings.fixPrompt: In `ui-v2/src/components/flows/flow-icon-text/flow-icon-text.stories.tsx`, `createTestRouter` passes `context: { queryClient: new QueryClient() }` to `createRouter` (around line 33). That client is never used, because `FlowIconText` reads the client from the `QueryClientProvider` in the decorator. Remove the `context` option, or check whether other stories in `ui-v2/src/components` use a shared pattern for this and follow it.

findings.title: Near-duplicate of FlowLink; consider a shared implementation
findings.fixPrompt: Consider consolidating `ui-v2/src/components/flows/flow-icon-text/flow-icon-text.tsx` with `ui-v2/src/components/flows/flow-link.tsx`. Either add a `showLabel` prop to `FlowLink` and have `FlowIconText` delegate to it, or extract a shared inner implementation that both use. Keep the existing `FlowLink` callers' behavior unchanged. This is optional if the team prefers separate components.

findings.title: Shared query, route, and icon wiring matches the established FlowLink pattern
findings.body: The implementation reuses `buildFLowDetailsQuery`, `useSuspenseQuery`, the `/flows/flow/$id` route (defined in `src/routes/flows/flow.$id.tsx`), and `Icon id="Workflow"`, which exists in `ui-v2/src/components/ui/icons/constants.ts`. These are the same choices `FlowLink` makes, so the new component will navigate and render consistently with existing UI. The `index.ts` re-export follows the other component folders.
